questions.explain: Straight line = linear; around a centre = circular; to and fro = oscillatory.

questions.prompt: Motion that repeats itself after a fixed time is called…
questions.explain: Periodic motion repeats at regular intervals, like a pendulum or the Earth's orbit.

questions.prompt: Adam and Priya sit in the same moving bus. Relative to Priya, Adam is…
questions.explain: They move together, so Adam's position doesn't change relative to Priya.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between circular and oscillatory motion?
options: Circular keeps going around in one direction; oscillatory goes back and forth
Circular motion is always in a straight line
questions.explain: Oscillatory motion reverses direction; circular motion doesn't.

questions.prompt: Which are examples of PERIODIC motion? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: A single kick doesn't repeat, so it isn't periodic.

questions.prompt: A bicycle moves along a straight road. What motion do its wheels show?
questions.explain: The wheels rotate while the whole bicycle moves in a straight line.

questions.text: An object is in motion if its ___ changes with time compared with a ___ point.
questions.explain: Motion = change in position relative to a reference point.

questions.prompt: Match each object to its type of motion.
questions.explain: Look at the path: around, to-and-fro, or straight.

questions.prompt: A passenger in a moving train says the trees outside are moving backwards. Is the passenger right? Explain using the idea of a reference point.
questions.modelAnswer: Relative to the passenger (the reference point), the trees are changing position and appear to move backwards, so from that reference point the statement makes sense. Relative to the ground, the trees are at rest and it is the train that is moving. Motion depends on the reference point chosen.
rubric: Relative to the passenger, the trees appear to move
Relative to the ground, the trees are at rest
Motion depends on the reference point
questions.explain: The same object can be moving or at rest depending on the reference point.
